newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close down 3.6 pct on poll jitters.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close down 3.6 pct on poll jitters.

text.p: French stocks slumped on Wednesday on talk that privately-commissioned polls showed the opposition Socialists well placed going into the parliamentary election runoff, brokers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 97.17 points, or 3.63 percent, to 2,583.17. The CAC-40 May futures contract fell 88 points to 2,590.
It was the second selloff on the bourse this week as investors priced in the risk that the Socialists, who won the first round last Sunday, could win on June 1, dealers said.
The CAC index lost 3.91 percent on Monday, then rebounded nearly one percent on Tuesday before poll rumours triggered fresh selling on Wednesday in very heavy turnover of 12.45 billion francs.

"We are seeing a follow-through from Monday. There has been a lot of complacency in the market and people did not take fully into account that the right could lose," said Merrill Lynch market strategist David Bowers.
The bourse is displaying the greatest volatility this week because it lagged the other markets in pricing in the risk of a Socialist victory, analysts say.

Equities are also seen as more vulnerable than bonds and the franc to a change in government. Analysts say the Socialists are unlikely to drop plans to join a single European currency but are more likely to block or delay structural reforms and sector restructurings proposed by the centre-right RPR-UDF coalition.
Shares in sectors due for restructurings were hit hardest.
* In the financial sector, BNP tumbled 7.13 percent to 233 francs, AGF fell 5.91 percent, Societe Generale tumbled 6.27 percent, Cie Bancaire fell 5.87 percent and Paribas dropped 5.28 percent.
* The car sector was also weak, with Renault down 7.89 percent at 133.10 francs and tyremaker Michelin off 4.44 percent at 325 francs.

* Privatisation stocks also took a beating on concerns a Socialist-led government might block or delay privatisations. Defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF fell 4.57 percent, bidders Lagardere and Alcatel Alsthom fell 4.61 percent and 5.26 percent, respectively.
Dassault Aviation, being merged with state-owned Aerospatiale, lost another 7.79 percent to 1,077 francs on fears Aerospatiale might not be privatised as planned.
* Building/public works firms outperformed. Bouygues fell 1.18 percent and its 59 percent owned unit Colas rose 5.98 percent. Lafarge lost 0.58 percent.

* LVMH also outperformed, closing down 1.63 percent at 1,389, after the group said it would exercise options to buy back Guinness's stakes in Moet Hennessy and the joint distribution ventures between the two companies.

The move is seen as a way to put pressure on Guinness and its merger partner Grand Met. Analysts say LVMH's objective is to create a group merging the Guinness-Grand Met drinks businesses with those of LVMH's Moet Hennessy drinks unit.
